classification.difficultyReason: Choose general coordinates, calculate opposite-side midpoints and use the hinted ratio to establish the same point on all three medians.

inlines.text: Use coordinate geometry to prove that the medians of any triangle are concurrent.
On each median find the coordinates of the point that divides the median in the ratio

answer.short:
The three medians meet at $G\left(\frac{a+c}{3},\frac{b}{3}\right)$ when the vertices are $O(0,0)$, $A(a,b)$ and $C(c,0)$.

Find the midpoint of each opposite side, then show that travelling two-thirds of the way along each median from its vertex gives this same point.
answer.worked:
Choose axes so that the vertices are $O(0,0)$, $A(a,b)$ and $C(c,0)$. Let $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be the midpoints of $AC$, $OC$ and $OA$, respectively. By the midpoint formula,
$$\begin{align*}X&=\left(\frac{a+c}{2},\frac b2\right),\\Y&=\left(\frac c2,0\right),\\Z&=\left(\frac a2,\frac b2\right).\end{align*}$$
A point dividing a median in the ratio $2:1$ from its vertex is two-thirds of the way from the vertex to the opposite midpoint. Its changes in both coordinates are therefore two-thirds of the corresponding total changes.

On median $OX$, this point is
$$\begin{align*}G_1&=\left(\frac23\cdot\frac{a+c}{2},\frac23\cdot\frac b2\right),\\G_1&=\left(\frac{a+c}{3},\frac b3\right).\end{align*}$$
On median $AY$, this point is
$$\begin{align*}G_2&=\left(a+\frac23\left(\frac c2-a\right),b+\frac23(0-b)\right),\\G_2&=\left(\frac{a+c}{3},\frac b3\right).\end{align*}$$
On median $CZ$, this point is
$$\begin{align*}G_3&=\left(c+\frac23\left(\frac a2-c\right),0+\frac23\cdot\frac b2\right),\\G_3&=\left(\frac{a+c}{3},\frac b3\right).\end{align*}$$
Thus all three medians contain the same point $G\left(\frac{a+c}{3},\frac b3\right)$, so they are concurrent.
